rationale: With the run at its wire I added the one artifact that still had value and could be written and validated inside the remaining minute: a synthesis entry that states, in one place and from the receipts rather than from prose scattered across three accounts, what the run established about the strength of the CheckQuorum lease. It records the two ways a healthy incumbent can be moved out of its lease - a message type the module only produces locally, and a vote request carrying the transfer marker - notes that both rest on the sender's honesty about its own state rather than on anything the receiver can check, and records the measurement that in both cases the cost to the incumbent is its term and its leadership rather than its ballot, because isUpToDate still applies after the term advance. That synthesis is the thing a reviewer of this audit would otherwise have to assemble from the parent account, the two boundary accounts and the transfer receipt, so it belongs in the index as its own fact.

knowledge.statement: The CheckQuorum leader lease binds only messages whose fields are honest, and this run measured two ways past it. First, a message type the module produces only locally: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg, so a peer-form message is accepted through both documented inbound paths, clears the follower's live leader context with no error and with either an unset or a legal term, and the identical pre-vote that the lease had withheld is granted afterwards. Second, a vote request carrying the CampaignTransfer marker: the lease is written as force := bytes.Equal(m.GetContext(), []byte(campaignTransfer)), so a marked higher-term request is not discarded at all and the receiver advances its term and becomes a follower. In both cases the receiving side holds no local check - no membership test, no term-value test, no record of a pending transfer - and in both the measured cost to a healthy incumbent is its term and its leadership rather than its ballot, because isUpToDate still guards the vote after the term advance: the forged-election receipt shows the incumbent answering neither request under its lease, and the transfer receipt shows it skipping the lease, adopting term 3, demoting to follower and rejecting the ballot.
knowledge.conditions: Config.CheckQuorum must be set, since otherwise inLease is always false and the lease suppresses nothing at all; the follower must hold a live leader context inside its election timeout; ReadOnlyLeaseBased refuses MsgForgetLeader outright, so that configuration is untouched. Evidence from both sides of the statement: indices 4 and 5 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 and indices 59 to 62 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624 for the first path, indices 12 and 16 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568 for the lease withholding both requests when no marker is present, and indices 66, 67 and 69 of CheckRun 026b6c86522d454299d1f3ca358c009e for the marker path with its demotion and rejection.
